name: MetricMeter
purpose: Record numeric measurements through four instrument shapes — counter, up-down counter, histogram, asynchronous gauge — under OpenTelemetry metric semantics.
invariants: Counter instruments MUST only accept non-negative values; negative deltas SHALL raise and are FORBIDDEN to be silently clamped.
Histogram boundaries MUST be finite, strictly increasing, and immutable once the instrument is created.
Instrument names MUST match the regex '^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_./-]{0,62}$' per OTel specification and CANNOT collide with a differently-typed instrument of the same name.
Every instrument MUST carry a UCUM unit string (e.g. 'ms', 's', 'By') — an empty unit is FORBIDDEN.
Observable gauge callbacks MUST be idempotent within a collection cycle and SHALL NEVER raise; exceptions are logged and the measurement is dropped.
Attribute sets attached to measurements NEVER include unbounded-cardinality keys (user id, request id, full URL path).
extension_contract: Downstream tools register a MetricReader adapter (pull-based Prometheus scrape or push-based OTLP exporter) and extend instrumentation by subclassing the meter provider to add a View that renames, filters, or re-aggregates instruments without mutating existing instrument contracts.

sources.locator: https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/histograms/ 'When to use which' and 'Errors of quantile estimation'

why_essential: Centralizing instrument creation is the only way to keep units, names, and attribute sets aligned across services; ad-hoc per-tool meters silently fork names and aggregations, making dashboards non-portable.
alternatives_considered: StatsD client per tool — rejected because it has no unit or description metadata and offers no histogram bucket control.
Prometheus client library directly — rejected because it binds code to pull-only collection and blocks push-based deployment models.
Pure log-derived metrics — rejected because aggregation at ingest is costly and loses millisecond-resolution histograms.
